summary: Assistance requested: enable aggressive batching + int8 quantization caused latency spikes and model regressions; need safe rollback plan
description: Issue summary: After applying Optimize suggestions (batch_size=64, aggregate=auto, quantize_profile=int8_aggressive, prefix_cache=true) customer saw request-level 500/502 errors and elevated end-to-end latency for text-generation flows. Impact: production service for PromptlyAI's assistant showing degraded quality (increased hallucinations) and tail latency spikes ~2.5x. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, model pinned to redwood-3b-8k-2026-02-quant; autoscaling enabled. Logs: provided below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Deploy model redwood-3b-8k-2026-02-quant to dedicated pool 'promptly-dedicated-us-east'.
2. Apply optimization profile: batch_size=64, max_batch_latency_ms=30, kv_prefetch=true, quantize=int8_aggressive, cache_prefix=true
3. Send multi-turn chat requests at 300 RPS, interactive prompts average 400 tokens
4. Observe increased 5xx at ~10-15m after rollout and higher token time per token
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:01Z ERROR serving-runtime request_id=... upstream=kernel-failure code=502 msg="kernel fallback failed"
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z WARN scheduler request_id=... batch_size=64 latency_ms=780 tail_p99=1240
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive int8 quantization may be introducing numerical instability for some layer types leading to runtime kernel fallbacks and increased decode latency due to fallback to slower paths.
Batching interaction: increased batch_size raises peak memory usage which can trigger host->device memory thrashing under contiguous request spikes.
KV/prefix cache: cache warming behavior could cause transient latency spikes; stale cache invalidation noted in logs at 14:11:50Z.
Checked dedicated GPU utilization: seen GPU at 92% during spikes; host OOM not observed but memory pressure high.
No immediate evidence of disk I/O saturation; network RTT stable in APM traces.
Related signal: trace shows kernel fallback to 'generic-attention' at 14:12:01 and repeated small kernel restarts for the same request id.
Repro attempt in staging with smaller batch sizes reproduced elevated latency but without 502s; suggests combined effect of quantization + high batch.
recommended_rollback_steps: 1) Pause rollout via Redwood Console: set model routing to previous stable variant redwood-3b-8k-2026-02 (non-quant) using Traffic Split.
2) Reduce batch_size to 8-16 and set max_batch_latency_ms to 100 while monitoring latency.
3) Revert quantize_profile to 'int8_safe' or disabled; prefer 'fp16' if available.
4) Flush prefix/KV cache for affected routes (Console -> Cache -> Invalidate prefix keys for 'assistant/*').
5) Restart a small subset of workers (canary) after config revert: use Dedicated -> Pools -> Instances -> Restart 2 workers.
6) Monitor for 30 minutes (latency/p99 and error rate) before rolling out further changes.
7) If immediate rollback not possible, apply temporary rate-limiting to reduce concurrency.
resolution: Workaround applied: Support instructed customer to set traffic back to redwood-3b-8k-2026-02 stable variant and lower batch_size to 12. Quantization profile rolled back to 'int8_safe'. After changes, error rate returned to baseline and p95 latency reduced from 650ms to 220ms within 20 minutes. Follow-up: Engineering to reproduce quantization regression in staging and open a runtime bug (INT-402). Proposed rollout checklist updated in Confluence.
follow_up_tasks: INT-402 run isolated replay of PromptlyAI workload with int8_aggressive profile
Create a safer 'canary' auto-rollback feature in Console (product/infra)
Add a preflight sim that estimates memory pressure for given batch/quant combinations
